styles.name: Precision Minimalism
styles.keywords: minimal clean calm professional content-first whitespace enterprise saas public service
styles.guidance: Use strong hierarchy, restrained surfaces, 1px borders, low shadow count, semantic tokens, and one clear accent. Let typography and spacing carry hierarchy.

styles.name: Bento Grid
styles.keywords: bento modular dashboard ai saas portfolio cards asymmetric modular responsive
styles.guidance: Use an intentional modular grid with varied card spans, clear alignment, and content-driven card sizes. Collapse to a single logical reading order on small screens.

styles.name: Editorial Narrative
styles.keywords: editorial publishing news culture campaign story report content typography
styles.guidance: Lead with typography, strong image rhythm, clear reading measure, sectional pacing, and restrained interactive chrome. Avoid dashboard-like card saturation.

styles.name: Operational Data Dense
styles.keywords: analytics dashboard admin operations monitoring finance enterprise table charts
styles.guidance: Optimize scanning: compact spacing, persistent labels, tabular numerals, stable table geometry, restrained color, explicit status semantics, and drill-down hierarchy.

styles.name: Soft UI Evolution
styles.keywords: wellness beauty hospitality lifestyle calm premium organic warm soft
styles.guidance: Use soft surfaces and gentle depth without low-contrast neumorphism. Keep form controls, focus states, and text contrast explicit.

styles.name: Neo Brutal
styles.keywords: bold youth creative campaign culture gaming high contrast poster expressive
styles.guidance: Use hard borders, oversized type, purposeful asymmetry, and limited high-contrast colors. Keep interaction semantics conventional and readable.

styles.name: Controlled Glass
styles.keywords: glassmorphism premium immersive media spatial dark translucent blur
styles.guidance: Use glass only for layered overlays or contextual surfaces. Measure composed contrast, keep blur purposeful, and provide opaque fallbacks.

styles.name: Dark Product UI
styles.keywords: dark developer cybersecurity ai media gaming terminal code
styles.guidance: Use near-black layered surfaces rather than pure black everywhere, high legibility, restrained luminous accents, and independent dark-mode contrast checks.

styles.name: Fluent 2 Inspired
styles.keywords: microsoft productivity enterprise windows office collaboration fluent
styles.guidance: Use layered neutral surfaces, clear command hierarchy, familiar controls, consistent tokens, and restrained motion suitable for productivity software.

styles.name: Material Expressive
styles.keywords: android material mobile consumer dynamic expressive cards app
styles.guidance: Use tokenized color roles, clear state layers, adaptive layout, platform-appropriate touch targets, and motion that explains hierarchy.

styles.name: Commerce System
styles.keywords: shopify commerce ecommerce merchant admin inventory checkout
styles.guidance: Prioritize trustworthy commerce patterns, predictable forms, clear monetary hierarchy, inventory state clarity, and conservative interaction behavior.

styles.name: Creative Tool System
styles.keywords: adobe spectrum creative editor design professional tool desktop
styles.guidance: Use dense professional controls, predictable panels, precise states, keyboard support, and strong selection/focus differentiation.

styles.name: Layered Platform Material
styles.keywords: apple ios macos liquid glass translucent native platform
styles.guidance: Use platform material only where it reinforces hierarchy. Respect system conventions, safe areas, legibility, and reduced-transparency preferences.

styles.name: Warm Humanist
styles.keywords: nonprofit social community healthcare education public civic trust human
styles.guidance: Use approachable typography, documentary imagery, generous spacing, plain-language actions, and calm trustworthy surfaces. Avoid charity clichés and manipulative urgency.

styles.name: Luxury Editorial
styles.keywords: luxury fashion hotel premium real estate beauty sophisticated serif
styles.guidance: Use refined serif display type, spacious composition, large art-directed imagery, subtle motion, and very limited accents. Preserve conversion clarity.

patterns.name: Outcome First SaaS
patterns.structure: Hero with measurable outcome and primary CTA -> trust proof -> problem/solution -> product workflow -> integrations -> evidence -> pricing/CTA -> FAQ.

patterns.name: Operational Dashboard
patterns.structure: Global context and filters -> KPI summary -> primary trends -> exceptions/actions -> detail tables -> drill-down. Keep priority actions above secondary metrics.

patterns.name: Service Booking
patterns.keywords: service spa beauty legal clinic booking appointment
patterns.structure: Value proposition + booking CTA -> services -> proof/credentials -> process -> testimonials -> availability/booking -> location/contact -> FAQ.

patterns.name: Commerce Conversion
patterns.structure: Category/value header -> discovery/filtering -> product proof -> product detail with price/availability/returns -> cart -> checkout with minimal friction and trust cues.

patterns.name: Editorial Story
patterns.keywords: news publishing report culture story campaign
patterns.structure: Strong title/deck -> lead visual -> readable narrative -> evidence/figures -> contextual modules -> related content -> clear next action. Avoid repetitive card grids.

patterns.name: Community Participation
patterns.keywords: nonprofit social civic community association membership donation
patterns.structure: Human outcome -> current need -> credible evidence -> ways to participate -> projects/impact -> transparency -> donation/member CTA -> contact.

patterns.name: Developer Product
patterns.keywords: developer api cli sdk technical security
patterns.structure: One-sentence utility -> install/try command -> capabilities -> working example -> docs/integration -> performance/security proof -> pricing or open-source CTA.

patterns.name: Portfolio Case Study
patterns.structure: Identity statement -> selected work -> case study outcomes -> capabilities -> process -> client proof -> contact. Let work lead; minimize decorative navigation.

patterns.name: Learning Journey
patterns.structure: Learner outcome -> audience fit -> curriculum/path -> instructor credibility -> sample content -> outcomes/testimonials -> enrollment CTA -> support/FAQ.

patterns.name: Trust and Compliance
patterns.keywords: finance healthcare government security insurance legal
patterns.structure: Primary service/value -> credentials and safeguards -> clear process -> detailed proof -> policies/FAQ -> human support -> action. Make risk and eligibility information easy to find.

charts.name: Line chart
charts.keywords: trend time series change over time continuous
charts.guidance: Use line for continuous trends. Keep series count low, direct-label when possible, and provide a table or textual summary.

charts.name: Bar chart
charts.guidance: Use sorted bars for categorical comparison. Start quantitative axes at zero unless a justified analytical exception is clearly signaled.

charts.name: Stacked bar
charts.keywords: composition part whole categories share percentage
charts.guidance: Use stacked bars when both totals and composition matter. Avoid too many segments and color-only differentiation.

charts.name: Histogram or box plot
charts.guidance: Use histogram for shape and box/violin for compact group comparisons. Explain outliers and sample size.

charts.name: Scatter plot
charts.guidance: Use scatter for relationships. Add trend line only when analytically justified; do not imply causation.

charts.name: Funnel or staged bars
charts.guidance: Prefer aligned staged bars with counts and rates over decorative funnel shapes. Make denominator changes explicit.

charts.name: KPI card plus context
charts.keywords: kpi metric headline number status summary
charts.guidance: Never show a naked number. Include period, comparison baseline, direction, unit, and accessible status text.

charts.name: Heatmap
charts.keywords: matrix calendar intensity density two dimensions
charts.guidance: Use only when ordered dimensions and intensity are the analytical question. Provide labels/tooltips and a non-color fallback.

charts.name: Map
charts.guidance: Use a map only when geography is analytically meaningful. Normalize choropleth values when comparing differently sized populations.

charts.name: Sankey
charts.guidance: Use for a small number of meaningful flows. Avoid when precise comparison matters more than flow structure.

charts.name: Timeline
charts.guidance: Use for ordered events and milestones, not for quantitative trends. Ensure readable date hierarchy and mobile reflow.

charts.name: Data table
charts.keywords: exact values dense compare records audit details
charts.guidance: Use tables when users need exact values, scanning, sorting, filtering, or copy/export. Keep columns prioritized and headers sticky only when helpful.

ux.name: Visible keyboard focus
ux.keywords: accessibility keyboard focus focus ring modal sticky
ux.guidance: Do not remove focus indication. Keep the focused control visible and unobscured by sticky UI or overlays.

ux.name: Contrast by role
ux.keywords: accessibility contrast text icon dark mode
ux.guidance: Target 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for meaningful non-text UI boundaries/icons. Test both themes independently.

ux.name: Pointer and touch targets
ux.keywords: touch target tap mobile pointer wcag
ux.guidance: Use platform minimums for native touch targets. On web, design generous targets and spacing; never rely on tiny glyph bounds.

ux.name: Forms and errors
ux.keywords: form validation error input label submit
ux.guidance: Use persistent labels, field-level errors, clear recovery, and an error summary when many fields fail. Preserve entered values.

ux.name: Reduced motion
ux.keywords: animation motion reduced motion transition
ux.guidance: Motion must explain state or hierarchy, not delay tasks. Respect reduced-motion preferences and keep final semantic state correct when animation is skipped.

ux.name: Responsive reflow
ux.keywords: responsive mobile overflow zoom text scaling layout
ux.guidance: Support narrow widths, zoom and enlarged text without clipping, horizontal page scroll, or hidden controls.

ux.name: Resilient text
ux.keywords: long text chip badge truncation wrapping localization
ux.guidance: Prefer wrapping. Let long tokens break safely. If truncation is unavoidable, provide an operable full-value path for keyboard, pointer and touch.

ux.name: Async feedback
ux.keywords: loading submit async progress skeleton latency
ux.guidance: Give immediate acknowledgement, prevent duplicate submission when needed, retain context, and distinguish loading from empty and error states.

ux.name: Predictable navigation
ux.keywords: navigation back breadcrumbs tabs deep link
ux.guidance: Back behavior, hierarchy and selected state must be predictable. Do not overload primary navigation with secondary destinations.

ux.name: Do not rely on color alone
ux.keywords: color state error success chart accessibility
ux.guidance: Pair functional color with text, icon, pattern or position. Ensure state remains understandable in grayscale and high contrast.

ux.name: Semantic icons
ux.keywords: icon aria label decorative accessible name
ux.guidance: Hide decorative icons from the accessibility tree. Standalone meaningful icons need text alternatives; icon buttons need accessible names and state.

ux.name: Stable perceived performance
ux.keywords: performance cls image lazy load skeleton layout shift
ux.guidance: Reserve media space, optimize noncritical assets, avoid layout shifts, split heavy features, and keep input feedback immediate.

ux.name: Density follows task
ux.keywords: density dashboard whitespace spacing hierarchy
ux.guidance: Dense operational screens can be compact; marketing and reading screens need more breathing room. Preserve a consistent 4/8-derived spacing system.

ux.name: Dark mode is not inversion
ux.keywords: dark mode theme tokens contrast
ux.guidance: Map semantic tokens per theme, use layered near-black surfaces, and tune accents/disabled states independently.

ux.name: Empty states are task states
ux.keywords: empty no data onboarding first run
ux.guidance: Explain why the state is empty and offer the next useful action. Do not fill empty states with decorative copy that hides the task.

ux.name: Destructive action safety
ux.keywords: delete destructive confirm undo irreversible
ux.guidance: Prefer undo for reversible actions. For irreversible actions, clearly name the object and consequence before confirmation.

ux.name: Accessible authentication
ux.keywords: authentication login password manager paste captcha
ux.guidance: Allow password managers and paste. Avoid cognitive puzzles as the only path and provide accessible recovery.

ux.name: Drag alternatives
ux.keywords: drag drop swipe gesture accessibility keyboard
ux.guidance: Every essential drag or swipe interaction needs a visible single-pointer and keyboard alternative.

ux.name: Localization resilience
ux.keywords: localization translation rtl long labels internationalization
ux.guidance: Do not size components to English strings. Support expansion, RTL where applicable, locale-aware dates/numbers, and flexible labels.

ux.name: Operational tables
ux.keywords: table data grid sort filter pagination responsive
ux.guidance: Use real headers and relationships, keyboard-operable controls, predictable column priority, and alternatives to horizontal overflow on small screens.

stacks.name: React
stacks.guidance: Keep state local, derive rather than duplicate state, stabilize expensive trees only when measured, and preserve semantic HTML.

stacks.name: Next.js
stacks.keywords: nextjs next.js app router server components
stacks.guidance: Prefer server rendering for static/data-heavy content, keep client boundaries narrow, stream meaningful sections, and optimize images/fonts through framework primitives.

stacks.name: Vue
stacks.guidance: Keep components focused, use computed state for derivation, preserve native semantics, and avoid unnecessary deep watchers.

stacks.name: Svelte
stacks.guidance: Use reactive primitives deliberately, keep DOM semantic, and avoid effects for values that can be derived.

stacks.name: Astro
stacks.guidance: Ship static HTML by default and hydrate only interactive islands. Keep content hierarchy and no-JS resilience strong.

stacks.name: HTML + Tailwind
stacks.guidance: Use semantic HTML first, reusable token classes/variables, responsive utilities intentionally, and avoid unreadable one-off class sprawl.

stacks.name: shadcn/ui
stacks.guidance: Compose primitives rather than restyling every part, preserve Radix semantics, centralize tokens, and verify focus/disabled/error states after customization.

stacks.name: Angular
stacks.guidance: Use standalone components and signals appropriately, keep templates semantic, and prefer framework control flow and change-detection-friendly patterns.

stacks.name: Nuxt
stacks.guidance: Use SSR and data composables deliberately, minimize client-only islands, and preserve accessible navigation during transitions.

stacks.name: Nuxt UI
stacks.guidance: Use the system tokens/components consistently before custom variants; verify accessible names, focus, contrast, and responsive overflow.

stacks.name: React Native
stacks.keywords: react native expo mobile ios android
stacks.guidance: Use platform semantics, safe areas, performant lists, correct accessibility props, and platform-specific touch behavior. Test text scaling.

stacks.name: Flutter
stacks.guidance: Use theme extensions/tokens, semantic widgets, adaptive controls where needed, efficient lists, and text scaling without hard-coded heights.

stacks.name: SwiftUI
stacks.guidance: Prefer native controls and semantic styles, Dynamic Type, safe areas, accessibility modifiers, and platform navigation conventions.

stacks.name: Jetpack Compose
stacks.guidance: Use Material semantics and tokens, remember state at the correct owner, lazy layouts for lists, and content descriptions only where meaningful.

stacks.name: Three.js
stacks.guidance: Treat 3D as enhancement, cap device pixel ratio, provide loading and reduced-motion strategies, keep primary tasks outside the canvas, and offer accessible equivalents.

stacks.name: Laravel
stacks.guidance: Keep server-rendered forms and validation semantic, progressive-enhance interactivity, and return errors adjacent to fields with preserved input.

stacks.name: JavaFX
stacks.guidance: Use native controls and CSS tokens, keyboard navigation, clear selection/focus, virtualized tables, and density suited to enterprise desktop work.

stacks.name: WPF
stacks.guidance: Centralize resources/styles, preserve automation properties, use virtualization, and make keyboard/focus behavior explicit.

stacks.name: WinUI 3
stacks.keywords: winui windows app sdk xaml fluent
stacks.guidance: Follow Fluent patterns, system backdrops where appropriate, keyboard/access keys, automation properties, and responsive window resizing.

stacks.name: Avalonia
stacks.guidance: Use theme resources and responsive layouts, preserve keyboard/focus semantics, and test platform differences rather than assuming WPF parity.

stacks.name: Uno Platform
stacks.guidance: Prefer shared semantic components with platform adaptation, central theme tokens, and verify input/focus across target platforms.

stacks.name: UWP Legacy
stacks.guidance: Treat UWP as legacy maintenance. Preserve accessibility and existing platform conventions; prefer migration planning for new strategic work.

quality_gates: One dominant visual and information hierarchy is evident within five seconds.
Normal text meets at least 4.5:1 contrast; meaningful non-text UI reaches 3:1 where applicable.
Keyboard focus is visible, logical, and not obscured; icon controls have accessible names.
Responsive behavior is checked at narrow mobile, tablet, desktop, zoomed text, and long-content conditions.
No essential interaction depends only on hover, color, drag, animation, or a tiny pointer target.
Loading, empty, error, disabled, success, permission, offline, and destructive states are intentionally designed where relevant.
Motion is purposeful, interruptible where needed, and has a reduced-motion behavior.
Typography, color, spacing, radius, elevation, icon sizing, and z-index are tokenized rather than arbitrary per component.
Charts answer a specific analytical question and have accessible text/table fallback when needed.
The final UI avoids generic AI tropes, decorative card saturation, fake urgency, and copy that competes with the primary task.
